raised.claim: The drift-guard test hardcodes its own list of columns and operators (plus extras like 'secret' and 'LIKE') instead of deriving the space from the source lists in triage-scope.ts.
raised.why_it_breaks: If a new column is added to NUMERIC_COLS/TEXT_COLS/NULLABLE_COLS or a new operator to one of the *_OPS in triage-scope.ts (and thus to a branch in SCOPE_TERM_JSON_SCHEMA), the pairs = cols.flatMap... will not contain any terms using the new identifier; a subsequent mismatch between tool schema and ScopeTermSchema for that identifier will produce no toolOnly or unreachable entries and the test will pass.

raised.claim: The drift-guard logic only checks existence of some probe value that zod accepts and some (possibly different) probe value that toolAdmits; it does not verify that the value constraints inside each anyOf branch exactly match the corresponding zod constraints.
raised.why_it_breaks: Changing the contains branch to { type: 'string', minLength: 5 } would still let toolAdmits return true for the probe 'matcher_bug' (length >=5) while zodOk is also true for it; both toolOnly and unreachable would stay empty, the test would pass, yet the tool schema would now reject a valid short contains term (e.g. {col:'name', op:'contains', value:'Cydr'}) that ScopeTermSchema would accept.
